full_text_en:
Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Shandong Branch v. Xincheng Co., Ltd. et al. — Dispute over Loan Contract

[Ruling Summary]

According to Article 48 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, where an enterprise establishes a new company with others by offsetting part of its property with an equal amount of debts, and does not hold corresponding shares in the transferred property, creditors of debts not transferred have the right to claim that the new company shall assume joint and several liability for the debts of the original enterprise to the extent of the property it received from the original enterprise.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court  
(2003) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 106

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shandong Xincheng Chemical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 132 Jinghe West Road, Tengzhou, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Zhicheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Hongwei, lawyer of Shandong Jinghe Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Shandong Branch, domiciled at No. 310 Jingsi Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.

Person in Charge: Du Baoqi, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Liu Hongbo, employee of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Shen Xiaowei, lawyer of Beijing Dingming Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Tengzhou Fertilizer Plant, domiciled at No. 132 Jinghe West Road, Tengzhou, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Ziying, Plant Manager.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jianhe, employee of the Plant.

Defendant at First Instance: Shandong Lunan Chemical Industry (Group) Company, domiciled at Mushi Town, Tengzhou, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Jianmin, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Tengzhou State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 86 Shanguo South Road, Tengzhou, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Lu Qingzhi, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Appellant Shandong Xincheng Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xincheng Company), in the case of dispute over loan contract with Appellee Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Shandong Branch (hereinafter referred to as Shandong Branch of ICBC), and Defendants at First Instance Tengzhou Fertilizer Plant (hereinafter referred to as Fertilizer Plant), Shandong Lunan Chemical Industry (Group) Company (hereinafter referred to as Lunan Company), and Tengzhou State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as State-owned Assets Company), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2001) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court, previously filed an appeal to this Court in 2002. After trial, this Court, on the ground that the facts were unclear, issued a civil ruling (2002) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 111 remanding the case to the Shandong High People's Court for retrial. After retrial, the Shandong High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2002) Lu Min Er Chong Chu Zi No. 1. Xincheng Company, being dissatisfied with the above judgment, again appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law, composed of Presiding Judge Wu Qingbao, Acting Judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min, with court clerk Kong Ling serving as recorder. This case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the original court upon retrial are as follows:

On August 26, 1996, Shandong Branch of ICBC and Fertilizer Plant entered into a medium- and long-term loan contract for RMB, numbered 1996 Ji Zi No. 0001, stipulating that Shandong Branch of ICBC would extend a loan of RMB 9,500,000 to Fertilizer Plant, with the loan term from August 26, 1996 to October 8, 1999. The actual date of drawing the loan was to be based on the loan receipt, which constituted a part of the contract. The loan interest rate was to be adjusted annually in accordance with state regulations; for the first year it was 6.675%, accruing from the date of disbursement by the lender, calculated on a daily basis and settled quarterly (monthly), with principal and interest due upon maturity. If the borrower failed to repay the loan principal and interest in accordance with the repayment plan agreed in the contract, the lender would charge interest on overdue loans at a daily rate of 0.04% as prescribed by the state; if interest was not paid on time, compound interest would be charged on the unpaid interest. If the lender failed to disburse the loan within five business days after the borrower completed the loan procedures, the lender would pay the borrower a penalty of 0.04% per day of the defaulted amount and days.

On May 27, 1997, Shandong Branch of ICBC and Fertilizer Plant entered into a medium- and long-term loan contract for RMB, numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006, stipulating that Shandong Branch of ICBC would extend a loan of RMB 29,000,000 to Fertilizer Plant for the purpose of technical transformation (repayment of previous technical transformation loan), with the loan term from May 28, 1997 to December 20, 1999. Lunan Company was to separately enter into a guarantee contract numbered Ji Zi No. 0006 to provide a guarantee to the lender. Other contents of this contract were the same as those of the loan contract numbered 1996 Ji Zi No. 0001.

On January 6, 1998, Shandong Branch of ICBC and Lunan Company entered into a guarantee contract using standard terms, numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006, stipulating that to ensure the performance of the contract numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006 entered into between Shandong Branch of ICBC and Fertilizer Plant, Lunan Company was willing to provide a guarantee to Shandong Branch of ICBC. The scope of guarantee covered the loan principal of RMB 29,000,000 borrowed by the borrower from Shandong Branch of ICBC under the loan contract and the interest thereon (including penalties, compound interest, and additional interest charged due to the borrower's default or overdue repayment, as well as the costs of realizing the claim). The performance period of the guaranteed loan contract was from January 1, 1998 to December 31, 1999. The guarantee period was two years, calculated from the date the borrower failed to perform the debt. The method of guarantee was joint and several liability guarantee. In the column of other matters, the parties agreed in non-standard terms that the guarantor would only assume the liability to repay the outstanding amount when the borrower was truly unable to repay.

After the above three contracts were signed, Shandong Branch of ICBC disbursed the said loan to Fertilizer Plant on October 9, 1998. Upon maturity of the loans, except for the payment of interest amounting to RMB 5,000,994.50 before September 20, 2001 (of which RMB 1,184,708.21 was paid under the loan contract numbered 1996 Ji Zi No. 0001, and RMB 3,816,286.29 was paid under the loan contract numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006), the loan principal and the remaining interest under both contracts were not repaid.

It was also found that on September 28 and December 14, 1999, the Shandong Provincial Commission for Economic System Reform approved, by letters Lu Ti Gai Qi Zi [1999] No. 117 and Lu Ti Gai Han Zi [1999] No. 75, the establishment of Xincheng Company jointly initiated by Fertilizer Plant, an employee stock ownership association, and several other investors. The total shares of the company were 40 million shares, with a par value of RMB 1 per share, and a total registered capital of RMB 40,000,000. Among them, Fertilizer Plant held 29.6 million shares, accounting for 74% of the total shares. On November 26 of the same year, the Capital Verification Report Run De Yan Zi (1999) No. J003 issued by Shandong Runde Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. stated that the registered capital applied for by Xincheng Company was RMB 40,000,000. As of November 25, 1999, Xincheng Company had received capital contributions from its shareholders totaling RMB 40,000,000. Among them, Fertilizer Plant contributed physical assets worth RMB 77,720,000 and transferred debts amounting to RMB 48,120,000 together with the physical assets. Fertilizer Plant's contribution was made by deducting the debts from the physical assets, resulting in net physical assets of RMB 29,600,000 as its capital contribution, with a contribution ratio of 74%. On December 22 of the same year, Xincheng Company obtained the "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person."

On December 28, 1999, Fertilizer Plant and Xincheng Company signed an agreement stipulating that Fertilizer Plant would transfer all of its assets valued at RMB 96,531,146.46 to Xincheng Company, and simultaneously transfer an equal amount of debts to Xincheng Company. Xincheng Company should actively repay the debts it had assumed under the agreement; Fertilizer Plant would no longer bear any joint and several liability for discharge of the debts transferred to Xincheng Company.

On January 10, 2000, Fertilizer Plant and Xincheng Company respectively entered into debt transfer agreements with seven financial institutions, including the Tengzhou Sub-branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the Business Department of Tengzhou Rural Credit Cooperative Union, Tengzhou Chengguan Town Rural Credit Cooperative, Tengzhou City Credit Cooperative, Tengzhou Xinggong City Credit Cooperative, Tengzhou Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China, and Shanting Sub-branch of Bank of China (hereinafter collectively referred to as the seven financial institutions including the Tengzhou Sub-branch of ICBC), agreeing to transfer debts totaling RMB 48,128,000 owed by Fertilizer Plant to the above seven entities to Xincheng Company.

Thus, Fertilizer Plant transferred property worth a total of RMB 174,251,146.46 and debts worth a total of RMB 144,651,146.46 to Xincheng Company. After the above asset transfers, Fertilizer Plant ceased production and operation, leaving a small number of personnel to handle legacy issues arising from the restructuring.

On September 26 of the same year, Fertilizer Plant and State-owned Assets Company signed an agreement stipulating that Fertilizer Plant would transfer the state-owned assets of RMB 29,600,000 it held to State-owned Assets Company for management and operation, and completed the procedures for amending the shareholder registration. State-owned Assets Company replaced Fertilizer Plant as a shareholder of Xincheng Company, holding 74% of the shares of Xincheng Company.

On September 25, 2001, Shandong Branch of ICBC filed a lawsuit with the Shandong High People's Court, on the grounds that Fertilizer Plant had failed to repay the loan principal and interest upon maturity, Lunan Company had not fulfilled its guarantee obligations, and Fertilizer Plant had stripped effective assets and established Xincheng Company to evade debts, requesting the court to order Fertilizer Plant, Lunan Company, and Xincheng Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 38,500,000, interest of RMB 11,527,023.25, as well as interest from September 20, 2001 to the date of payment, other costs of realizing the claim, and litigation costs. On November 6 of the same year, Shandong Branch of ICBC submitted a "Supplemental Complaint" to the Shandong High People's Court, on the ground that Fertilizer Plant had transferred its assets of RMB 29,600,000 to State-owned Assets Company without consideration, and State-owned Assets Company had taken over 74% of the equity of Xincheng Company held by Fertilizer Plant, applying to add State-owned Assets Company as a co-defendant in the case and requesting that it be ordered to bear joint and several liability for repayment to Shandong Branch of ICBC. After the Shandong High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2001) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 1, Xincheng Company, being dissatisfied, appealed to this Court. During the second instance trial of this Court, Shandong Branch of ICBC submitted to this Court a photocopy of the "Agreement" entered into between Fertilizer Plant and Xincheng Company on January 1, 2000. The photocopy of the agreement stated that, in addition to the capital contribution of RMB 29,600,000, Fertilizer Plant also transferred to Xincheng Company certain fixed assets, current assets, etc., that should be transferred according to the needs of fertilizer production, using the method of assuming equal debts, with net assets transferred amounting to RMB 127,074,372.95 and liabilities of RMB 127,074,372.95. The ownership of the above transferred assets belonged to Xincheng Company, and the transferred liabilities were to be repaid by Xincheng Company; Fertilizer Plant would no longer bear them. The above contributed assets and assets assumed with equal debts were all delivered to Xincheng Company from 0:00 on January 1, 2000. The remaining assets and liabilities of Fertilizer Plant were to be held by Fertilizer Plant, which would bear the obligation to repay the liabilities. At the same time, Shandong Branch of ICBC submitted to this Court the "Balance Sheet" of Xincheng Company as of January 31, 2000, to prove the authenticity and actual performance of the above "Agreement" and requested that Xincheng Company be ordered to bear all debts of this case. Xincheng Company and Fertilizer Plant both did not recognize the photocopy of the above "Agreement." This Court, on October 8, 2002, issued civil ruling (2002) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 111, on the ground that the facts were unclear, remanding the case to the Shandong High People's Court for retrial.

The Shandong High People's Court upon retrial held: The two loan contracts entered into between Shandong Branch of ICBC and Fertilizer Plant, as well as the guarantee contract entered into between Shandong Branch of ICBC and Lunan Company, were the true expressions of intent of the parties and did not violate laws or administrative regulations; they were all valid contracts. After the contracts were signed, Fertilizer Plant completed the loan procedures on October 9, 1998, and Shandong Branch of ICBC disbursed all the loans under the two contracts to Fertilizer Plant on the same day. Therefore, it should be determined that Shandong Branch of ICBC had performed its obligations under the two loan contracts. Upon maturity, Fertilizer Plant failed to repay the loan principal and interest as agreed, constituting a breach of contract, and it should bear the liability for default for overdue repayment of loan principal and interest. The guarantee contract signed by Lunan Company and Shandong Branch of ICBC clearly stated that it was to provide a guarantee for the loan under the contract numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006 entered into between Shandong Branch of ICBC and Fertilizer Plant, and the loan purpose was to repay the technical transformation loan. Lunan Company's claim that it did not know the loan was a new loan to repay an old one and should be exempted from liability was inconsistent with the facts, and the court did not accept it. Although the method of guarantee liability agreed in the guarantee contract was joint and several liability guarantee, because the agreement was a standard term, and the parties subsequently agreed in a non-standard term that Lunan Company only assumed the liability to repay the outstanding amount when the borrower was truly unable to repay, it should be determined that the guarantee provided by Lunan Company to Shandong Branch of ICBC was, in nature, a general guarantee. When Fertilizer Plant was unable to repay the loan principal and interest under the contract numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006, Lunan Company should bear the guarantee liability to Shandong Branch of ICBC. Xincheng Company, as a new company established by Fertilizer Plant together with others, accepted assets of Fertilizer Plant amounting to RMB 48,120,000 by assuming debts at the time of its establishment, and after its establishment, it accepted assets of Fertilizer Plant amounting to RMB 96,531,146.46 in the same manner (the total of the two sums being RMB 144,651,146.46). Fertilizer Plant formed Xincheng Company with others using its high-quality assets, thereby causing itself to lose its production capacity and debt-servicing ability. Xincheng Company should bear joint and several liability for Fertilizer Plant's debts to the extent of the property it received from Fertilizer Plant, which was RMB 144,651,146.46. After Xincheng Company was established, before Fertilizer Plant had cleared its debts, Fertilizer Plant transferred its equity in Xincheng Company to State-owned Assets Company without consideration, which was evidently an act of evading debts. State-owned Assets Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts owed by Fertilizer Plant to the extent of the 74% equity in Xincheng Company it received. The court, in accordance with Article 90 and Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 41 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 17 and Article 21 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 39 and Article 42 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Disputes Related to Enterprise Restructuring (hereinafter referred to as the Judicial Interpretation on Enterprise Restructuring), decided:

1. Fertilizer Plant shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, repay to Shandong Branch of ICBC the loan principal of RMB 9,500,000 under the contract numbered 1996 Ji Zi No. 0001 and the corresponding interest (the interest during the contract term shall be calculated at the interest rate agreed in the contract, the overdue interest shall be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China, and the interest of RMB 1,184,708.21 already paid by Fertilizer Plant shall be deducted);

2. Fertilizer Plant shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, repay to Shandong Branch of ICBC the loan principal of RMB 29,000,000 under the contract numbered 1997 Ji Zi No. 0006 and the corresponding interest (the interest during the contract term shall be calculated at the interest rate agreed in the contract, the overdue interest shall be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China, and the interest of RMB 3,816,286.29 already paid by Fertilizer Plant shall be deducted);

3. Lunan Company shall bear general guarantee liability for Fertilizer Plant's debts determined in Item 2 above;

4. Xincheng Company shall, within the scope of RMB 144,651,146.46, bear joint and several liability for discharge of Fertilizer Plant's debts determined in Item 1 and Item 2 above;

5. State-owned Assets Company shall, within the scope of its 74% equity in Xincheng Company, bear joint and several liability for discharge of Fertilizer Plant's debts determined in Item 1 and Item 2 above.

Court acceptance fee for first instance of RMB 260,145 and property preservation fee of RMB 148,000 shall be borne by Fertilizer Plant.

Xincheng Company, being dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shandong High People's Court, appealed to this Court, alleging that: Fertilizer Plant formed a new company with others by contributing physical assets of RMB 77,720,000 and corresponding debts of RMB 48,120,000, rather than forming a new company with others by contributing its high-quality assets, which fully conforms to the circumstances stipulated in Article 6 of the Judicial Interpretation on Enterprise Restructuring. Fertilizer Plant has not lost its ability to repay debts or its production capacity. The court of first instance erroneously conflated two distinct legal acts: Fertilizer Plant's unilateral restructuring act of contributing physical assets of RMB 77,720,000 to the appellant and transferring debts of RMB 48,120,000 together with the physical assets, and the bilateral civil juristic act of transferring assets of RMB 96,531,146.46 and equal debts to the appellant after the appellant was established. Moreover, as of the present, the appellant has already repaid the vast majority of the debts it accepted. Even if Shandong Branch of ICBC believed that the method of transferring assets and debts together between Fertilizer Plant and the appellant was illegal and infringed upon its legitimate rights and interests, it could only request the court to revoke the act. According to Article 6 of the Judicial Interpretation on Enterprise Restructuring, since the appellant has already repaid the debts of RMB 48,120,000 in full, Fertilizer Plant's act of restructuring into a company should be protected by law. The court of first instance, despite having found that the appellant had already repaid Fertilizer Plant's debts within the scope of the property it had accepted, still ruled that the appellant should bear joint and several liability for discharge of the debts owed by Fertilizer Plant to Shandong Branch of ICBC within the scope of the property it had accepted, thereby increasing the burden on the appellant. The findings of fact by the court of first instance were unclear, and the application of law was improper. It requested that the judgment be amended according to law, and that the claim of Shandong Branch of ICBC against the appellant be dismissed.

Appellee Shandong Branch of ICBC responded that: When Fertilizer Plant was restructured, in addition to contributing property of RMB 77,720,000 to form Xincheng Company with others, it further transferred assets of RMB 96,539,146.46 to Xincheng Company within a week after Xincheng Company was established, thereby causing Fertilizer Plant to lose its operating capacity and debt-servicing capacity. The court of first instance correctly ruled that Xincheng Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts of Shandong Branch of ICBC within the scope of the property it had received, on the ground that Fertilizer Plant had formed Xincheng Company with others using its high-quality assets during the restructuring. The appellant's claim that the acts of transferring assets by Fertilizer Plant to Xincheng Company at the time of and after the establishment of Xincheng Company were legal acts of a different nature had no legal basis. Fertilizer Plant did not notify Shandong Branch of ICBC of the asset transfers. Fertilizer Plant, under the pretext of restructuring, stripped the enterprise's high-quality assets to achieve the purpose of evading debts. The findings of fact by the court of first instance were clear, and the application of law was correct. The judgment should be affirmed.

Defendant at First Instance Fertilizer Plant made no written statement, but at the trial expressed agreement with the opinion of Xincheng Company. Defendant at First Instance Lunan Company stated in writing that the findings of fact by the court of first instance were clear and the application of law was correct, but that when ruling that it should bear general guarantee liability, the court did not clearly grant it the right of recourse. It requested that the court of second instance clarify this.

In addition to the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court on second instance also found that: the debt owed by Fertilizer Plant to Shandong Branch of ICBC, which is the subject of this dispute, was not included in the debts transferred by Fertilizer Plant to Xincheng Company.

Opinion of the Court:

The loan legal relationship between Shandong ICBC and the Fertilizer Plant and the guarantee legal relationship between Shandong ICBC and Lunan Company are clear, both representing the true intentions of the parties and not violating the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; therefore, they should be valid. The parties have no objection to this. The main issue disputed in this appeal is whether Xincheng Company, established after the restructuring of the debtor Fertilizer Plant, bears civil liability for the debts of the Fertilizer Plant incurred prior to the restructuring.

In 1999, the Fertilizer Plant jointly established Xincheng Company with the Plant's employee shareholding association and several other investors. The Fertilizer Plant initially contributed tangible assets of RMB 77.72 million to Xincheng Company, while simultaneously transferring liabilities of RMB 48.12 million, using the net assets of RMB 29.6 million (after offsetting tangible assets against liabilities) as its capital contribution to Xincheng Company, representing a 74% shareholding. Subsequently, it entered into an agreement with Xincheng Company to transfer high-quality assets worth RMB 96,531,146.46 along with an equal amount of debt to Xincheng Company. The two parties agreed that Xincheng Company would be responsible for repaying these two debts totaling RMB 144,651,146.46, which were transferred together with the tangible assets. Since the agreement between the Fertilizer Plant and Xincheng Company regarding the transfer of the above debts does not violate mandatory legal provisions, represents the true intentions of the parties, and complies with the principle of autonomy of will, the agreement should be valid among the transferor, the transferee, and the creditors of the transferred debts, provided that the creditors of the transferred debts have no objection. However, as all property of an enterprise constitutes general security for all debts arising from its operations, no one may arbitrarily transfer it. The law grants creditors the right to obtain satisfaction of their claims equally from all legal person property, and no one enjoys privileges except creditors with priority rights. That is, the realization of one creditor's claims cannot be secured at the expense of sacrificing the claims of another creditor. Therefore, although the relevant debt transfer agreements reached by the Fertilizer Plant with Xincheng Company and relevant creditors are legally binding on the parties to the agreements, the act of Xincheng Company receiving the corresponding property as consideration for assuming the transferred debts objectively resulted in a reduction of the Fertilizer Plant's legal person property that serves as security for all creditors' claims. This property transfer infringed upon the rights of other creditors. The agreement between the Fertilizer Plant and Xincheng Company, regarding the precondition of assuming equal debts in exchange for receiving the relevant property, has no legal effect on other creditors. When Shandong ICBC, as a creditor whose debt was not transferred, requires Xincheng Company to assume liability for repayment of the Fertilizer Plant's pre-restructuring debts within the scope of the property it received from the Fertilizer Plant, based on the principle of legal person property, Xincheng Company shall not use its agreement with the Fertilizer Plant to oppose Shandong ICBC's claims. By transferring property and equivalent debts to form a new company with others, the Fertilizer Plant did not obtain corresponding equity interests in the transferred property; thus, this act is not genuinely an investment but a disguised transfer of legal person property.

Whether the Fertilizer Plant lost its ability to repay debts and to conduct production after restructuring to form a new company is not the basis for determining whether Xincheng Company should bear liability for the Fertilizer Plant's pre-restructuring debts. Therefore, Xincheng Company's appellate argument that the Fertilizer Plant did not lose its ability to repay debts or to produce, and thus Xincheng Company should not bear the Fertilizer Plant's debts, is not supported by this Court. The legal nature of the Fertilizer Plant's act of transferring legal person property worth RMB 144,651,146.46 to Xincheng Company is clear. Therefore, Xincheng Company's appellate argument that the two property transfers were not legal acts of the same nature is also not supported by this Court.

Article 6 of this Court's Judicial Interpretation on Restructuring, which provides that "Where an enterprise uses part of its property and corresponding debts to form a new company with others, and the creditors approve the transferred debts, the newly formed company shall bear civil liability," applies only to creditors whose debts are transferred, and does not include creditors whose debts are not transferred. That is, if a restructured enterprise transfers debts to a newly formed company, and the transfer is approved by the relevant creditors, the legal consequence of an effective debt transfer occurs, and the newly formed company bears the transferred debts. If a restructured enterprise transfers debts without the consent of the creditors of the transferred debts, the legal consequence of debt transfer does not occur, and the debts remain with the restructured enterprise. If a restructured enterprise transfers part of its property to a newly formed company, then under the principle of legal person property, the newly formed company shall bear joint civil liability with the restructured enterprise to the extent of the property received. Creditors whose debts are not transferred still have the right, under the principle of relativity of contract and the principle of legal person property, to demand that the restructured enterprise and the new company receiving the restructured enterprise's property assume corresponding repayment liability. Therefore, Xincheng Company's appellate argument that it has already lawfully assumed certain debts of the Fertilizer Plant and should not bear the debt owed to Shandong ICBC is likewise not supported by this Court.

Shandong ICBC's claim that Xincheng Company should bear liability for the debt in dispute to the extent of the property it received from the Fertilizer Plant has a legal basis and is supported by this Court. The original court's judgment that Xincheng Company shall bear joint and several liability for discharging the debts of the Fertilizer Plant incurred prior to the restructuring, to the extent of the property received from the Fertilizer Plant, is affirmed by this Court. If, after repaying this debt to Shandong ICBC, Xincheng Company suffers an imbalance in its rights and obligations, it may separately assert claims against the Fertilizer Plant. Lunan Company, after assuming the guarantee liability, has the right to seek recourse against the debtor. As the Security Law already provides clear provisions on this matter, this Court will not address it in this second-instance judgment.

Pursuant to Article 48 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1), and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 260,145; property preservation fee: RMB 148,000, to be borne by Tengzhou Fertilizer Plant. Court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 260,145, to be borne by Shandong Xincheng Chemical Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao

Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

Acting Judge: Liu Min
